name: where_order_paging
comment: The kitchen sink: top-level where entries AND implicitly; parameters number @c0.. in render order — WHERE first, then limit, then offset, on every dialect, even where the rendered clause reorders them (OFFSET @c5 before FETCH @c4); property names resolve to columns through the metadata.

sqlite.sql: select id, name, email, display_name, created_at, updated_at from users where ((id = @c0 or name in (@c1, @c2)) and created_at >= @c3) order by name desc, id limit @c4 offset @c5

sqlserver.sql: select [id], [name], [email], [display_name], [created_at], [updated_at] from [users] where (([id] = @c0 or [name] in (@c1, @c2)) and [created_at] >= @c3) order by [name] desc, [id] offset @c5 rows fetch next @c4 rows only
